section.catchline: Definitions -- Assessment of real property subject to a low-income housing covenant.
section.subsection:
As used in this section:
"Lease up period" means the period that begins the day on which residential housing located on real property subject to a low-income housing covenant is available for occupancy and ends the day on which the residential housing achieves 90% occupancy for a continuous three-month period. "Low-income housing covenant" means an agreement: between:
the Utah Housing Corporation or a government entity; and an owner of real property upon which residential rental housing is located; in which the owner described in Subsection (1)(b)(i)(B) agrees to limit the amount of rent that a renter may be charged for the residential rental housing; and that is filed with the county recorder in the county in which the real property is located. "Residential rental housing" means housing that: is used:
for residential purposes; and as a primary residence; and is rental property.

subsection.subsection:
A county assessor shall, in determining the fair market value of real property subject to a low-income housing covenant: use the income capitalization approach, if the county assessor finds that the income capitalization approach is a valid indicator of the property's fair market value; in using the income capitalization approach:
calculate the property's net operating income using the reduced rent amounts that result from the low-income housing covenant; and during the lease up period, account for rent loss due to vacancy and lease up costs; and take into account all other relevant factors that affect the fair market value of the property, including the information provided in accordance with Subsection (3).
Subject to Subsection (2)(b)(ii), Subsection (2)(a) applies regardless of whether the property is complete or under construction.

For a property under construction, when determining fair market value under this section, the county assessor shall take into account the impact of the low-income housing covenant on the fair market value of the property.

If the April 30 described in Subsection (3)(a) occurs before occupancy of the property or before the end of the lease up period, the property owner shall provide estimates of the information required by Subsections (3)(a)(ii) and (iii).

On or before March 31 each year, the county assessor shall send a copy of the form described in Subsection (3)(a) to each owner of real property subject to a low-income housing covenant located in the county.

section.subsection:
If an owner of real property subject to a low-income housing covenant fails to meet the requirements of Subsection (3):
the assessor shall: make a record of the failure to meet the requirements of Subsection (3); and make an estimate of the fair market value of the property in accordance with Subsection (2) based on information available to the assessor; and subject to Subsection (5), the owner shall pay a penalty equal to the greater of: $250; or 5% of the tax due on the property for that year.

subsection.subsection: Only one penalty per year may be imposed per housing project subject to a low-income housing covenant.
Upon making a record of the action, and upon reasonable cause shown, an assessor may waive, reduce, or compromise the penalty imposed under Subsection (4)(b).
An owner is not subject to a penalty under Subsection (4) for a year in which the county assessor failed to timely comply with Subsection (3)(c).
